newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore public housing resale market stabilises.
newsitem.headline: Singapore public housing resale market stabilises.

text.p: The resale market for Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats, Singapore's public housing, has stabilised in the third quarter, newspapers said on Saturday.

Citing data provided by HDB, the newspapers said average valuations for all HDB estates rose just 4.4 percent in the third quarter, lower than the 9.6 percent and the 5.5 percent increases in the first and second quarters respectively.
The average valuation of three-room flats was S$156,000 (US$110,600). It was $272,100 for four-room flats, $408,500 for five-room flats and $527,600 for executive flats.
Industry sources said the HDB data showed the once buoyant resale market had flattened out, one newspaper said.
Prices had almost come to their peak and were tapering off, as anticipated by the government, Homemaster Realty director Chong Kek Mun was quoted by the Business Times as saying.
The paper said property agents gave the cause as the introduction of executive condominiums.
They agents also said the quieter resale market was a reflection of sentiment towards the private property market which was hit by the government's introduction of anti-speculation curbs in mid-May.
The range of measures included the introduction of a property gains tax and stamp duties for properties sold within three years of their purchase dates.
HDB has yet to release resale transaction volumes which had already fallen in the second quarter by 11 percent to 8,992 compared with the previous quarter, according to a newspaper report.
